data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 fails the problem's core demand by providing no causal mechanism that is measurable within a single evaluation, nor any evidence that would distinguish genuine reliability from mere compliance. It relies on a generic edge-case/lossy-compression narrative but never identifies what observable signal within one evaluation would separate a panel correctly catching an anomaly from a checklist that merely happens to cover the anomaly. The claim that the expert recognizes 'signatures' is asserted, not operationalized—there is no test for determining, within a single evaluation, when the expert's intuition is a genuine reliability gain versus a coincidental match.
